summary.short: Colorado HB 24-1130 adds C.R.S. 6-1-1314 and biometric definitions to the Colorado Privacy Act. From July 1, 2025, controllers collecting biometric identifiers must give notice, obtain consent and keep a written retention and security policy; they may not sell or lease such identifiers or refuse service for withholding consent.
summary.long: HB 24-1130 adds C.R.S. 6-1-1314 and biometric definitions to Part 13 of the Colorado Privacy Act, and amends its applicability provision. Controllers that control or process biometric identifiers must adopt a written policy with a retention schedule, incident protocol and deletion guidelines; processors need an incident protocol. Before collecting, controllers must inform consumers of the purpose and retention period and obtain consent. Controllers may not sell, lease or trade biometric identifiers, may disclose them only as listed, may not refuse service for withholding consent or charge different prices for exercising Part 13 rights, and must protect them to the industry standard of care. Consumers may request free disclosure of sources, purposes and recipients from entities meeting listed thresholds. Employers may require consent as a condition of employment only for listed purposes such as secure access and recording work hours. Part 13 applies to controllers doing business in Colorado or targeting residents that meet consumer-count thresholds, and to any controller processing any amount of biometric identifiers. Effective July 1, 2025, subject to a referendum petition. The text contains no penalty provisions.

enforcement.note: The section heading of added C.R.S. 6-1-1314 refers to 'remedies and civil actions', but no remedies, penalty or civil-action provision appears in the fetched text. Subsections (1) to (7) contain definitions, duties, employer consent rules and a Department of Law rulemaking power (subsection (7)), but no sanction. The text covers only the bill's sections 1 to 5, and the fetched text does not cite the enforcement provisions of the Colorado Privacy Act.
